Keywords: Court recognition and the scope of commands
RagShortTexts: Princely court visits cost travel, gifts and waiting.
Recognition of rank differs from permission to travel.

Variants.Content: A prince seeking recognition brings gifts and attendants and waits for audience. Instructions then travel home. Rank, passage and a specific levy are different authorities whose effect depends on recipients and local power.
Credential bearers identify proper recipients and carry supplies. Passage at one stage does not ensure every remount at the next; improvised demands cause delays.
Recognition requires explaining real obligations to cities and retainers. Exaggerating a document’s scope may intimidate rivals but discredits promises that cannot be supplied.
Court journeys impose local costs and returning demands. Acknowledged payments matter because distant recognition cannot recreate depleted household stores.
